result.evidence: The reproduction breaks at the premise that ht-qhz.1 cannot complete until the peer actor-routing implementation is available. The root's Immutable identities and owned interfaces assigns this leaf topology types and 'inert dispatch/signatures'; the leaf itself says 'Land only compilable additive BootstrapPlan/DeliveryPlan, state/result types and inert protocol/CLI/journal dispatch wiring' and 'inert-by-default compiles' with 'no topology effect or speculated human shortcut.' This permits a neutral contract and refusing/inert execution boundary without importing an unlanded InvocationActor implementation. Its actor-classification ordering contract does not authorize runnable new retry before that integration; the root requires original classification before every retry, and ht-qhz.19 plus ht-qhz.20 verify that ordering and guard integration before finished delivery. Thus ht-qhz.3 and ht-qhz.2.1 depending on the owned topology contract does not establish that unavailable actor source stalls those deliverables. The actual explicit peer-source gate is the human recovery integration: CLI and compatibility requires its approved dispatch contract before the recovery leaf is edited, and ht-qhz.6 names that source gate. Separately ht-qhz.2.1 expressly waits for actual reviewed migrations 0026/0027 before editing 0028, while independent ready work proceeds. The finding identifies a possible overly broad implementation of the seam task, but cannot complete the claimed failure story against 'only actual blocking shared boundaries gate their integration leaf, no global HOLD' without treating inert contract wiring as mandatory live actor integration.
